title: Inside the Standard Library: flatMap
hints: The closure returns a whole sequence per element; you need to concatenate them.
Make the method generic over `S: Sequence` and return `[S.Element]`.
jsBridge: Same as JS `flatMap`: map each element to a sequence, then concatenate. Swift's generic signature `<S: Sequence>(…) -> [S.Element]` accepts any sequence type, not just arrays.

compass.q: JS `flatMap` only flattens one level of arrays. Is Swift's the same?
Can the transform return a `String` (a sequence of `Character`s)? What would you get?
Flattening sections into rows for a list is flatMap. Where else?
